evidenceHint.en: The appointment file for each in-scope seat filled during the period, holding the assessment against the written standard and the approver's decision on any shortfall.

text.en: Obtain the current competence standard for the seat before the appointment is confirmed.
Assess the candidate or internal mover against each element of that standard and note the gaps.
Agree the supervision, training or withheld duties that cover a gap until it is closed.
File the assessment and the approver's decision with the appointment record.

title.en: Re-test the standards against the period's process and system changes

description.en: Where a process, system or reporting requirement changed in the period, judge whether the competence stated for the seats it touched is still the competence the work now demands.

text.en: Compile the process, system and reporting changes of the period that touched an in-scope control.
Map each change to the seats whose control it altered, using the control matrix as the link.
Compare the stated requirement for those seats against what the changed control now demands.
Revise the affected standards, or record why the existing wording still holds.
Report the seats left with an out-of-date standard to the control owner with a date to fix.

templates.title: Pre-hire screening performed for control-relevant roles
templates.description: Background checking completed before a person takes up a control-relevant post, with the depth of check set by the authority and access that post carries.
templates.objective: To ensure a person appointed to a control-relevant post has been screened to a depth matched to the authority the post carries, and cleared before they can act on it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control-relevant post is graded into a screening tier from the approval limit, system privilege and data access it holds.
Each appointment into such a post in the period holds a completed screening result dated before the start date.
The checks reach contractors, agency staff and internal movers into these posts, not only external permanent hires.
An adverse or incomplete result was decided by the person entitled to decide it, with the outcome recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the tiering schedule showing each control-relevant post, its graded tier and the attributes the grade was drawn from.
Obtain the screening procedure, including the checks each tier attracts and the consent and retention rules they run under.
Draw the appointment population for the period from payroll joiners, contractor and agency records, and internal transfer lists.
Obtain the screening file for each sampled appointment and the start date recorded for the same person.
Obtain the log of adverse or incomplete results and the decision recorded against each.

Analysis:
Test every appointment into the highest tier and a sample of the lower tiers, so depth is judged where the authority sits.
Compare the checks actually performed against the checks the post's tier required, and note any performed at a lower tier.
Set each clearance date against the start date to find people who began work before the checks returned.
Trace internal movers into a higher-tier post to a re-screening, rather than reliance on the clearance held for their previous seat.
Test the adverse results for a recorded decision by the named decider, and check any restriction imposed was applied in the systems.

Output:
Schedule of the period's appointments with the tier, the checks held and the clearance date for each.
List of people who started before clearance, or who hold checks below their post's tier, with the authority each was granted meanwhile.
Statement of whether adverse results were decided by the entitled decider and whether restrictions were enforced.

title.en: Grade each control-relevant post by the authority it carries

description.en: Place every post that performs, reviews or can override a control into a screening tier, using the money, data and system authority it holds rather than its position in the hierarchy.

text.en: Take the posts that perform or approve an in-scope control from the control matrix.
Note for each post its approval limit, its system privileges and the data it can reach.
Assign a tier from those attributes, so a junior post that releases payments sits above a senior post that cannot.
Agree the tiering with Legal/Compliance so each check is lawful where the post is hired.

title.en: Define the check set each tier of post attracts

description.en: Fix which checks a tier requires, from identity and right to work through to qualification verification, references, credit and criminal record, and the consent and retention rules that govern them.

text.en: Specify the checks applying at every tier, such as identity and right to work.
Add the checks only the higher tiers attract, naming the authority that triggers them.
State the consent, disclosure and retention rules each check runs under, per jurisdiction.
Name the provider or internal team performing each check and the turnaround it commits to.
Appoint who decides when a result is adverse or incomplete, and what they are entitled to decide.

title.en: Complete the tier's checks before the appointee takes the seat

description.en: Run the checks the post's tier requires and clear them ahead of the start date, holding the start or the authority rather than letting a person begin on trust.

evidenceHint.en: The screening file for every appointment in the period, showing each check the tier required, its result, and the clearance date set against the recorded start date.

text.en: Begin the checks when the offer is made, so turnaround does not force a start on trust.
Note each check returned, its result and its date, against the tier the post was graded at.
Hold the start date, or withhold the post's authority, where a required check has not returned.
File the screening result so its clearance date can later be compared with the start date.

title.en: Escalate an adverse or incomplete result to the named decider

description.en: Where a check returns something adverse or cannot be completed, route it to the person entitled to decide and capture what they decided and why, rather than letting the appointment proceed by default.

evidenceHint.en: The adverse-result log for the period, each entry carrying the decision to proceed, restrict or withdraw, the decider's name and the date it was taken.

text.en: Route the result to the decider named for that tier within the time the procedure states.
Assemble what the decider needs: the check returned, the post's authority and any explanation offered.
Capture the decision to proceed, to restrict the post's authority, or to withdraw the offer.
Apply any restriction in the systems that grant the post its authority, not on paper alone.
Dispose of the adverse result at the end of the retention period set for it.

title.en: Sweep the period's appointments for a missing or under-tiered check

description.en: Take every person who took up a control-relevant post in the period, whether external hire, contractor, agency worker or internal mover, and test each against the file their tier should have produced.

text.en: Draw the appointment population from payroll joiners, contractor records and transfer lists.
Match each appointment to a screening file and set out those with none.
Check the checks performed match the tier the post carries rather than a lower tier.
Test whether an internal mover into a higher tier was re-screened for the seat moved into.
Refer the exceptions to an owner with a date, and escalate anyone still in post uncleared.

templates.title: Onboarding covers the role's control responsibilities
templates.description: What a new or moved post-holder is walked through before performing a control: the controls the seat owns, the evidence each must leave, and where its authority stops.
templates.objective: To ensure a person taking up a control-relevant seat is walked through the controls it owns and the evidence they must leave, before they first perform one of them.
templates.successCriteria:
Each control-relevant seat has an onboarding brief naming the controls it performs, the evidence each leaves and the authority limit that binds it.
Every joiner and internal mover into such a seat in the quarter completed the brief, with a dated record of who delivered it.
The brief was delivered before the holder first performed the control, not at the close of a probation period.
Where a seat's controls changed since the brief was written, the version delivered reflects the change.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the onboarding brief held for each control-relevant seat, with its version date and the control set it was written from.
Draw the quarter's population of joiners and internal movers into those seats from HR records, transfer lists and contractor onboarding records.
Obtain the completed brief for each sampled person, showing the deliverer, the holder's acknowledgement and the date.
Obtain the date each sampled person first performed one of the seat's controls, taken from the control evidence itself.
Collect the changes made to the seats' control sets during the quarter.

Analysis:
Reconcile the seat population against the briefs held to expose control-relevant seats with no brief written at all.
Test every sampled person for a completed brief, and compare its delivery date with the date of their first performance.
Sample briefs and trace their content back to the current control matrix, checking the controls, evidence and limits named are the seat's own.
Compare the version delivered against the version current at the delivery date, to catch a superseded brief still in use.
Test whether contractors and internal movers were briefed on the same basis as permanent joiners.

Output:
Schedule of the quarter's entrants to control-relevant seats, with the brief date and first performance date for each.
List of people who performed a control before being briefed, naming the control performed.
List of seats with no brief, or with a brief predating the last change to the seat's controls.

title.en: Determine what each control-relevant seat must brief its holder on

description.en: Decide per seat which controls its holder performs, what evidence each must leave and the limit beyond which they escalate, so the brief is built from the seat rather than a generic induction pack.

text.en: Pull from the control matrix the controls each in-scope seat performs or reviews.
State the evidence each of those controls must leave and where it is filed.
Name the authority limit the seat holds and who it escalates to beyond that point.
Note the system access the seat needs and the segregation rule constraining it.

title.en: Build the onboarding brief for each seat from its control set

description.en: Turn the per-seat content into something a line manager can deliver, with a checklist showing what was covered and a record that the seat's holder received it.

text.en: Draft one brief per seat, covering its controls, the evidence they leave and its limits.
Include the date by which the holder is expected to perform each control unaided.
Add a sign-off for the deliverer and the holder, with the date of delivery.
Attach the underlying procedure or work instruction rather than restating it in the brief.
Agree with HR where the completed brief is filed so it can be produced on request.

title.en: Deliver the brief before the holder first performs the control

description.en: Walk the new or moved holder through the seat's brief ahead of their first performance, and capture the delivery rather than relying on a manager's recollection of it.

evidenceHint.en: The completed onboarding brief for each joiner and internal mover in the quarter, signed by the deliverer and the holder and dated ahead of the first performance.

text.en: Schedule the briefing inside the seat's stated window, ahead of the first performance date.
Walk the holder through each control, the evidence it leaves and the limit that binds it.
Capture the questions raised that show the brief is unclear, and send them to its author.
File the signed brief with the joiner record and note the date it was delivered.

title.en: Trace the quarter's joiners and movers to a completed brief

description.en: Take the quarter's population of people who entered a control-relevant seat and test whether each holds a delivered brief dated before they first performed one of the seat's controls.

text.en: Draw the quarter's joiner and internal-mover population from HR and contractor records.
Filter it to those entering a seat that performs or reviews an in-scope control.
Match each to a completed brief and compare its date with the first performance of the control.
Sample the briefs against the current control set to confirm the version delivered was current.
Report the seats briefed late or not at all, naming the control performed meanwhile.

templates.title: Annual role-specific training completion tracked
templates.description: The yearly training each control-relevant role is required to complete, tracked against a named population so a non-completion is visible rather than assumed away.
templates.objective: To ensure the training each control-relevant role must complete in the year is tracked against a named population, so a person who has not completed it is visible before the year closes.
templates.successCriteria:
A module set is assigned per control-relevant role rather than one course issued to everyone, and each role maps to the modules it requires.
The tracked population is drawn from the establishment and includes contractors and internal movers, not only the permanent staff in post at the year's start.
Completion is held per person and per module with a date, and the register separates not started from overdue.
Every non-completion reached a conclusion in the year: completed, waived by a named approver, or escalated to the role's owner.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the curriculum map showing each control-relevant role and the modules assigned to it.
Obtain the completion register as at the year end, holding a status and date per person and per module.
Obtain the establishment of control-relevant roles at the year end, with the joiners, leavers and internal movers of the year identified.
Collect the chase correspondence and the approved waivers or deferrals recorded against non-completions.
Obtain the completion rate as reported to management for the year.

Analysis:
Reconcile the enrolled population against the year-end establishment in both directions, and explain every name appearing on only one side.
Sample people across preparer, reviewer and approver roles and confirm each was assigned the module set their role requires.
Recompute the completion rate from the register and compare it with the rate reported, noting whether waived entries were counted as complete.
Test the joiners and internal movers of the year for enrolment from the date they entered the role, not from the following cycle.
Trace each non-completion to its conclusion, and check a waiver was approved by someone entitled to grant it.

Output:
Schedule of control-relevant roles with the module set assigned to each, naming those with none.
Reconciliation of the enrolled population against the establishment, with the unexplained names on each side.
Recomputed completion rate against the reported figure, and the list of non-completions still open at the year end.

title.en: Assign the module set each control-relevant role must complete

description.en: Decide what each role is required to learn in the year, distinguishing the role that performs a control from the one that approves it, instead of routing everyone to a single course.

text.en: Group the in-scope roles by the control work they do, not by department or grade.
Select the modules each group must complete, naming the control risk each addresses.
Add the modules a change in the year makes necessary, such as a new system or reporting requirement.
Set the completion deadline for each module and the year it runs to.

title.en: Load the curriculum and its deadlines into the training record

description.en: Put the per-role assignment into the system that holds completion, so a person's outstanding modules can be read off a register rather than assembled by hand at the year end.

text.en: Enrol each role's population against its assigned modules in the learning record.
Configure the deadline and the reminder schedule for every enrolment.
Link the enrolment to the HR establishment feed so a joiner or mover is picked up automatically.
Sample people against the modules their role requires, to prove the register was built correctly.

title.en: Chase the outstanding completions to a dated conclusion

description.en: Work the list of people who have not completed, during the year rather than after it, until each is completed, formally waived, or escalated to the role's accountable owner.

evidenceHint.en: The year-end completion register showing each person's status per module, with the chase correspondence and any waiver approved by a named manager.

text.en: Run the outstanding list at each reminder point and send it to the line manager.
Capture the reason given for each non-completion, such as leave, transfer or workload.
Route a request to waive or defer to the manager entitled to approve it, and note the decision.
Escalate the people still outstanding at the deadline to the role's accountable owner.
Close each entry as completed, waived or escalated, with the date it reached that state.

title.en: Test the completion register against the establishment at year end

description.en: Reconcile the population the register tracked against the people actually holding control-relevant roles at the year end, so a role never enrolled does not read as fully compliant.

text.en: Draw the establishment of control-relevant roles at the year end from HR records.
Compare it with the enrolled population and explain every name on only one side.
Recompute the completion rate from the register and compare it with the rate reported.
Check contractors and internal movers were enrolled from the date they entered the role.
Report the roles with no module set assigned and the people holding none at all.

templates.title: Control responsibilities included in performance objectives
templates.description: The duty to operate a control is written into the objectives of the individual who performs it, so the responsibility rests on a person and not on a function.
templates.objective: To ensure each person who operates a control carries that duty in their agreed objectives for the period, so accountability sits on a named individual rather than on a team.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control in the register resolves to a named individual whose objectives for the period state the duty.
The objective wording names the control and when it falls due, rather than committing generally to compliance.
People who joined or changed role during the period had objectives amended within the window the cycle sets.
Where a control changed hands, the duty was closed out of the outgoing holder's objectives and added to the incoming holder's.
No objective names a control that has since been retired from the register.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the control register for the period showing the owner recorded against each control.
Obtain the objective records agreed at cycle start for every person named as an owner.
Obtain the joiner and internal-move report for the period from the HR system.
Obtain the stated window for setting objectives after a hire or a change of role.
Request the ownership change log for controls that moved between holders.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register's owner column against the objective population and isolate controls whose holder has no objective naming the duty.
Read a sample of at least 25 objectives, or all of them where fewer, for a stated act and a due date rather than a general undertaking.
Compare each internal move against the date the objectives were amended and measure the gap against the stated window.
For each control that changed hands, check the outgoing holder's duty was removed and the incoming holder's added in the same cycle.
Search the objective set for duties naming controls no longer in the register.

Output:
An exception list of controls whose named holder carries no objective covering them.
The gap in days for every joiner or mover whose objectives were amended late.
A statement of the sample size, the population drawn from, and the exceptions found.

title.en: Resolve every control in the register to one named individual

description.en: Take each control down to a single person rather than a department, because an objective can only be written for an individual and a duty shared between several is the one nobody performs.

text.en: Export the control register with its owner column as it stood at the opening of the objective cycle.
Resolve each owning team or function to a single named person who actually performs the work.
Flag controls sitting against a vacant post or a shared mailbox and escalate them for assignment.
Record the person-to-control mapping with the date it was taken, as the population for the cycle.

title.en: Draft objective wording that states the duty and when it falls due

description.en: Agree a form of words specific enough to be assessed at the end of the period, so that an evaluator can decide whether the duty was discharged or not.

text.en: Write wording that names the control, the act required of the holder, and the date it is due.
Separate that duty from a general commitment to compliance, which cannot be judged at year end.
Agree the wording with the process owners whose objectives will carry the duty this cycle.
Load the agreed wording into the objective-setting template used across the organization.

title.en: Amend objectives when a control changes hands mid-cycle

description.en: Move the duty with the control whenever somebody joins, leaves or transfers, so the register and the objective records do not drift apart between cycles.

evidenceHint.en: The amended objective records for the outgoing and incoming holders, each dated, alongside the ownership change log entry they answer.

text.en: Watch the joiner, leaver and internal-move feed for people entering or leaving a control role.
Amend the incoming holder's objectives to name the control within the window the cycle sets.
Close the duty out of the outgoing holder's objectives so it is not counted against two people.
Note the effective date of each amendment against the entry in the ownership change log.

title.en: Sweep the register mid-cycle for controls with no matching objective

description.en: Check the two records against each other partway through the period, while an unassigned control can still be given to somebody before the cycle closes.

evidenceHint.en: The dated comparison showing register holders without an objective covering the duty, and objectives naming controls no longer in force.

text.en: Pull the objective records in force at the sweep date for everyone named as a holder.
Identify controls whose holder carries no objective naming the responsibility at all.
Identify objectives naming a control that has since been retired from the register.
Refer each unmatched control to the executive owning that function for reassignment.
Report the count of unmatched controls and the days taken to clear each one.

templates.title: Performance evaluations assess control responsibilities
templates.description: At the close of the cycle, the evaluation of each control holder carries a judgement on how the control was actually operated, supported by what the period's records show.
templates.objective: To ensure the control duties agreed at the start of the cycle are judged in the completed evaluation against the period's recorded results, rather than passed over or rated on impression.
templates.successCriteria:
Each completed evaluation for a control holder carries an explicit judgement on the control duty, not only on functional targets.
The judgement cites what the period recorded: completions, exceptions, overdue remediation or test results.
Holders whose controls failed repeatedly are rated differently from holders whose controls operated as designed.
Where the duty was judged unmet, a consequence or development action is recorded against the holder.
Evaluations are signed within the window the cycle sets, and any outstanding one is named.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the completed evaluation records for everyone who held a control duty during the period.
Obtain the control test results, exception logs and overdue remediation items covering the same period.
Obtain the evaluation calendar stating when ratings were due and signed.
Collect the consequences or development actions recorded where a duty was judged unmet.
Request the calibration notes for ratings adjusted after moderation.

Analysis:
Read a sample of at least 25 evaluations, or all where fewer, for a judgement that addresses the control duty by name.
Set each holder's rating against the failures recorded on their own controls, and isolate holders rated as meeting the duty whose controls failed more than once.
Trace a rating comment back to the exception log or test result it cites, to confirm the cited evidence exists.
Compare signature dates against the evaluation window to find ratings completed late or not at all.
Check each unmet judgement carried an action, and whether that action was afterwards performed.

Output:
A list of control holders whose evaluation contains no judgement on the control duty.
The set of holders rated favourably despite recorded control failures, naming the failures.
A statement of evaluations outstanding at the cut-off and how many days they are overdue.

title.en: Set the criteria a control duty judgement has to meet

description.en: Decide in advance what an evaluator must cite and what separates a duty discharged from one only partly discharged, so ratings across evaluators mean the same thing.

text.en: State the evidence an evaluator must cite, such as test results, exception counts or overdue items.
Define what separates a discharged duty from a partly discharged one in terms an evaluator can apply.
Agree how a control failure outside the holder's influence is treated, so the rating stays fair.
Publish the criteria to evaluators before the rating window opens for the cycle.

title.en: Build the control duty section into the evaluation form

description.en: Put the judgement where the evaluator cannot skip it, and place the holder's objectives and period evidence in front of them at the moment they write it.

text.en: Add a field to the evaluation template requiring a judgement on the control duty in words.
Make that field mandatory so a form cannot be submitted while it is left blank.
Show the holder's agreed objectives and the period evidence inside the same form.
Pilot the form with a small group of evaluators and correct the wording they misread.

title.en: Rate each holder's control duty on the period's recorded results

description.en: Write the rating from what the evidence pack shows rather than from recollection, and raise an action where the duty was not discharged.

evidenceHint.en: Completed evaluation forms carrying the duty judgement, each citing the test result, exception log entry or overdue item it rests on.

text.en: Read the period evidence attributed to the holder before drafting any rating text.
State the judgement in the evaluation, citing the specific result or exception it rests on.
Distinguish holders whose controls operated from those whose controls failed repeatedly.
Raise a development action or a consequence where the duty was not discharged.
Sign and date the evaluation inside the window the cycle calendar sets.

title.en: Challenge favourable ratings given to holders of failed controls

description.en: Take the ratings that contradict the period's record to moderation before they are finalised, since an unchallenged one teaches everybody that the duty is decorative.

evidenceHint.en: The moderation record listing each rating challenged, the control failures behind the challenge, and the outcome after the evaluator responded.

text.en: Join the rating table to the control failures recorded against each holder for the period.
Select every holder rated as meeting the duty whose controls failed more than once.
Ask the evaluator what evidence supported that rating, and record the answer given.
Refer unexplained cases to the moderation forum before ratings are finalised.
Summarise the challenges raised and their outcome for the cycle's record.

templates.title: Incentive structures reviewed for override pressure
templates.description: The pressure a reward scheme places on the people it pays: targets, thresholds and payout curves examined for what they would reward somebody for doing to figures that person helps prepare.
templates.objective: To ensure the payout terms of every scheme in force are examined each cycle for the pressure they place on participants able to influence the figures their reward is measured on.
templates.successCriteria:
Every scheme in force is listed with its metric, threshold, payout curve, cap and participant population.
Each metric is traced to the account, estimate or judgement a participant is positioned to influence.
Schemes carrying a cliff edge, uncapped upside or a single period-end measure are identified and the reason recorded.
Participants settling within a narrow band of a threshold are examined against their period-end activity.
Conclusions are passed to the owner of the fraud risk assessment rather than held within the reward function.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scheme documents in force for the period, with targets, thresholds, payout curves and any discretion held.
Obtain the participant population for each scheme and the measure each person is paid against.
Obtain the actual results by participant at the measurement date, showing where each landed relative to threshold.
Collect the malus, clawback or conduct gate terms and every occasion they were applied.
Obtain the minutes recording who reviewed the schemes and what was concluded.

Analysis:
Map each metric to the accounts and estimates a participant can influence, separating figures they prepare from figures set elsewhere.
Identify cliff structures where a small movement in the measure changes the payout sharply.
Select participants landing within a narrow band of a threshold and examine the transactions booked on their metric near the cut-off.
Test whether a conduct gate or clawback could be applied in practice, not merely stated in the terms.
Compare the conclusions reached against the fraud scenarios on record, to confirm the pressure identified reached that assessment.

Output:
A schedule of schemes ranked by the pressure their terms create, with the reason recorded against each.
The participants who settled close to a threshold and what examination of their period-end activity showed.
A statement of which conclusions were passed to the fraud risk assessment and which changes to scheme terms were proposed.

title.en: Assemble a schedule of every reward scheme and who is paid under it

description.en: Bring each bonus, commission and long-term award operating in the period onto one schedule, since a scheme nobody has written down is a scheme nobody examines.

text.en: Gather the terms of every bonus, commission and long-term award in force during the period.
Record the metric, threshold, payout curve and any cap that applies to each of them.
List the participants under each scheme and the measure their payout depends upon.
Note where discretion can change a payout, and which person or body holds it.

title.en: Trace each scheme metric to the figures its participants prepare

description.en: Establish where the person being paid also influences the number deciding the payment, which is the condition that turns a reward into pressure on a control.

evidenceHint.en: The metric-to-account mapping for the cycle, marking every measure whose inputs are prepared or approved by the participant being paid on it.

text.en: Take each metric from the scheme schedule and name the ledger account or estimate behind it.
Mark the metrics whose inputs are prepared or approved by the participant being paid.
Flag measures resting on a judgement, such as a reserve, an accrual or a cut-off date.
Rank the schemes by how far a participant is able to move their own measure.
Hand the ranking to the reviewing body as the basis for this cycle's discussion.

title.en: Examine payouts that settled within a narrow band of a threshold

description.en: Look at the population where the pressure would have shown itself, comparing what was booked near the cut-off for those who just cleared a threshold and those who just missed one.

evidenceHint.en: The near-threshold schedule for the cycle, showing each selected participant, the period-end transactions examined and the conclusion reached.

text.en: Compute each participant's distance from the nearest threshold at the measurement date.
Select those landing just above a threshold and those falling just short of one.
Examine the transactions booked on their metric in the closing days of the period.
Ask the process owner to explain anything timed unusually close to the cut-off.
Record the conclusion for every case selected, including those where nothing was found.

title.en: Attach a conduct gate to schemes whose terms allow none

description.en: Give the organization a route to withhold or recover a payout won in a way it would not defend, because a scheme paying on the number alone rewards the override as readily as the result.

text.en: Identify schemes whose terms offer no route to withhold or recover a payment.
Draft gate wording tying payment to how the result was reached, not to the number alone.
Agree that wording with the body approving reward terms before the next cycle opens.
Amend the scheme documents and tell participants what changed and when it takes effect.

title.en: Refer the pressure findings into the fraud risk assessment

description.en: Pass what the examination found to the people who build fraud scenarios, so the pressure this control identifies becomes an input there instead of being assessed twice or not at all.

evidenceHint.en: The dated transfer note listing each scheme concern handed over, with the fraud register entry or scenario it was logged against.

text.en: Summarise each scheme concern as what its terms would reward somebody for doing.
Send that summary and the supporting schedule to the owner of the fraud risk assessment.
Confirm each concern was logged as a scenario input, or record why it was not taken.
Keep the transfer note so the two assessments can be reconciled at the year end.

templates.title: Financial reporting objectives defined and approved
templates.description: A written statement of what the financial reporting is required to achieve - the framework applied, the entities consolidated, the dates fixed and the precision expected - approved by those accountable for it.
templates.objective: To ensure the reporting framework, consolidation boundary, calendar and precision the financial statements must meet are stated in writing and approved before the period they govern.
templates.successCriteria:
A written statement of financial reporting objectives exists, naming the accounting framework and the version of it in force for the period.
The consolidation boundary is drawn, with every legal entity either included or excluded on a recorded basis.
The calendar fixes close, review and filing dates, each carrying the person accountable for meeting it.
The statement carries a dated approval, and the approver held that authority on the date given.
Changes in framework, group structure or filing obligation since the prior period are reflected rather than carried forward unamended.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved statement of financial reporting objectives in force for the period, with the minute recording its approval.
Obtain the legal entity register at period end - the population against which the consolidation boundary is tested.
Collect the reporting calendar issued to the finance team and the register of filing obligations.
Request the prior period statement and the change log between the two versions.
Obtain the delegated authority schedule covering the approver at the approval date.

Analysis:
Compare the framework named in the statement against the framework actually applied in the accounting policies note.
Reconcile the entity register to the consolidation boundary in full rather than on a sample, and confirm each exclusion carries a stated basis.
Sample six fixed dates from the calendar across two closes and judge whether each was met, revised or missed.
Set the approval date against the start of the period to confirm the objectives were fixed before the reporting they govern.
Trace each change identified since the prior period through to the current statement.

Output:
Whether an approved statement exists for the period, naming its approver and the date of approval.
Schedule reconciling the legal entity register to the consolidation boundary, with unexplained entities on either side.
Statement of whether approval preceded the period governed, and by how far it lagged if not.
List of framework, structure or filing changes that never reached the current statement.

title.en: Establish the accounting framework and the entities reported on

description.en: Settle the two upstream facts every later judgement depends on: which accounting framework the statements are prepared under, and which legal entities fall inside the reporting boundary.

text.en: Name the accounting framework and the version of it in force for the reporting period.
Draw the consolidation boundary from the legal entity register, marking each entity in or out.
State the basis for every exclusion, so a reader can test it rather than infer it.
Identify the filing obligations the objectives must satisfy, covering regulator, exchange and lender reporting.

title.en: Set the calendar and the precision each reporting output must meet

description.en: Turn the objectives into dates and tolerances a finance team can work to, distinguishing what statutory reporting demands from what internal management reporting needs.

text.en: Fix the close, review, approval and filing dates for every reporting output in the period.
Name the individual accountable for each date rather than the department that holds it.
State the precision expected of each output, separating statutory from management reporting.
Circulate the draft calendar to component controllers so an unachievable date is challenged before approval.

title.en: Obtain approval of the objectives before the period opens

description.en: Put the statement to the body or officer holding the authority to fix it, and get an approval that names the version approved and the date it was given.

evidenceHint.en: The minute or written resolution approving the statement, carrying its date and identifying the version it approved.

text.en: Submit the statement to the board, audit committee or officer holding delegated authority.
Check that authority against the delegated authority schedule as it stood on the approval date.
Obtain the minute or resolution and confirm it identifies the version that was approved.
Issue the approved statement to component controllers and the external reporting team.

title.en: Challenge the objectives against what the period actually reported

description.en: Look back at the closed period and judge whether the objectives held: whether the filings made matched the obligations named, whether the boundary followed the group as it changed, and whether the dates were achievable.

text.en: Compare the filings actually made against the obligations the statement named.
Identify entities acquired, disposed or made dormant since approval and test whether the boundary followed.
Assess whether revised or missed dates point to a calendar that was never achievable.
Refer proposed amendments to the approver with the reason each one is needed.

templates.title: Materiality thresholds determined and documented
templates.description: The amounts at which a misstatement begins to matter, derived from a named benchmark by a stated rule, set below that figure for aggregation risk, and revisited when the benchmark itself moves.
templates.objective: To ensure the thresholds that decide whether a misstatement matters are derived from a named benchmark by a documented rule, and are re-derived when that benchmark moves.
templates.successCriteria:
Overall materiality is expressed as a stated percentage of a named benchmark, and that figure traces to reported numbers.
The choice of benchmark is justified by who relies on the reporting, and any change from the prior period carries a reason.
Performance materiality and a clearly trivial threshold sit below the overall figure, each with the rule that derives it.
Circumstances that make a sub-threshold amount material are listed, covering covenant, related party and remuneration items.
A tolerance for movement in the benchmark is defined, and a move beyond it produced a re-derivation within the period.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the materiality memorandum in force at each reporting date in the period, with the benchmark figure it used and the source of that figure.
Obtain the reported results for every reporting date in the period, not the year end alone - that set is the population.
Collect the derivation working showing the percentage applied and the arithmetic behind each figure.
Obtain the schedule of unadjusted differences accumulated against the clearly trivial threshold.
Request the list of qualitative circumstances that override the amount, and any item escalated under one.

Analysis:
Trace the benchmark figure at each reporting date to the statements or management accounts it was drawn from.
Re-perform the arithmetic behind the overall, performance and clearly trivial figures.
Compare the benchmark actually reported against the figure in use and test whether movement beyond the tolerance produced a re-derivation.
Sample fifteen accumulated differences and check that items above the trivial threshold were carried rather than discarded.
Test the qualitative list against the period's covenant, related party and remuneration arrangements for a circumstance it does not cover.

Output:
Re-performed derivation for each reporting date, with any difference from the documented figure.
Whether benchmark movement triggered the re-derivation the tolerance required, and how long the stale figure stood.
Schedule of unadjusted differences identifying items wrongly treated as trivial.
Circumstances present in the period but absent from the documented qualitative list.

title.en: Choose the benchmark the thresholds will be derived from

description.en: Pick the figure readers of the statements actually judge the entity by, and write down why it fits better than the alternatives considered.

text.en: Identify who relies on the reporting and the figure those readers judge the entity by.
Compare candidate benchmarks - revenue, pre-tax profit, total assets, total expenditure - for stability over three periods.
Select one and state why it fits this entity's readers better than the alternatives.
Name the statement and line the benchmark figure will be taken from at each reporting date.

title.en: Derive the overall, performance and trivial figures

description.en: Apply the rule to the benchmark and show the arithmetic, including the haircut taken for aggregation risk and the floor under which differences need not be collected.

text.en: Apply the chosen percentage to the benchmark figure and show the arithmetic in the working.
Set performance materiality below the overall figure and state the aggregation risk it absorbs.
Fix the clearly trivial threshold under which a difference need not be accumulated.
Define the movement in the benchmark that will force the figures to be derived again.
Draft the list of circumstances that make a sub-threshold amount material regardless of size.

title.en: Accumulate the period's differences against the trivial threshold

description.en: Collect every difference the close throws up, judge each against the trivial figure, and set the running total against performance materiality rather than against the overall figure.

evidenceHint.en: The closed schedule of unadjusted differences for each reporting date, each line showing its amount, the figure it was judged against and the decision taken.

text.en: Capture each difference the close identifies, whether it was corrected or left standing.
Judge each against the clearly trivial figure and carry forward those above it.
Total the carried items and set the aggregate against performance materiality.
Escalate items meeting a qualitative circumstance to the CFO whatever the amount.
Close the schedule at each reporting date and file it with the close pack.

title.en: Retest the thresholds after the benchmark itself has moved

description.en: The failure this catches is a threshold that ran a whole period on a benchmark the business had already moved away from, leaving scoping and evaluation decisions resting on a stale number.

text.en: Compare the benchmark reported at each period end against the figure the thresholds were derived from.
Measure the movement against the defined tolerance and state whether a re-derivation was required.
Check that any re-derivation reached the scoping and evaluation decisions that depend on it.
Report to the CFO every period in which a stale benchmark stood behind the thresholds in use.

templates.title: Significant accounts and disclosures scoped annually
templates.description: The annual selection of the ledger accounts and financial statement disclosures that internal control over financial reporting will cover, tested against the thresholds and against risk factors, with the exclusions recorded.
templates.objective: To ensure the accounts and disclosures taken into scope for internal control over financial reporting are chosen each year against the thresholds and stated risk factors, with exclusions reasoned.
templates.successCriteria:
Scoping begins from a complete population: a trial balance at a stated date reconciled to the financial statements, plus the disclosure index of the latest filing.
Every line carries both a quantitative result against the threshold and a qualitative result against the stated risk factors.
Sub-threshold lines brought into scope name the factor that carried them, and excluded lines name the reason.
In-scope accounts are mapped through to the processes, locations and assertions behind them.
Excluded balances are totalled and the aggregate is set against performance materiality.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the trial balance at the scoping date and its reconciliation to the financial statements - that reconciled population is the denominator for everything below.
Obtain the disclosure index of the most recent filing, the population for narrative items.
Collect the completed scoping matrix showing the quantitative and qualitative result recorded against each line.
Obtain the mapping from in-scope accounts to processes, locations and assertions.
Request the approval of the final scope and the comparison against the prior year's scope.

Analysis:
Reconcile the matrix line count back to the trial balance to confirm nothing was dropped before any test was applied.
Re-apply the quantitative threshold across the whole population and compare the resulting set with the documented in-scope list.
Sample ten accounts excluded on size and test whether estimation, judgement, related party volume or fraud susceptibility should have carried them in.
Total the excluded balances and set the aggregate against performance materiality.
Follow a sample of eight in-scope accounts through the mapping to a named process, location and assertion.

Output:
Reconciliation of the scoped population to the financial statements, with any gap quantified.
Re-performed threshold run listing accounts in scope under the test but missing from the documented scope.
Aggregate of excluded balances set against performance materiality.
Schedule of scope movements from the prior year, with the reason recorded against each addition and removal.

title.en: Draw the account and disclosure population from the ledger

description.en: Build the denominator before any judgement is applied: the trial balance reconciled to the statements, plus the disclosure index, fixed at a stated date.

text.en: Extract the trial balance at the scoping date and reconcile it to the financial statements.
Add the disclosure index from the latest filing so narrative items are scoped alongside balances.
Split balances carried at more than one entity or location into their component parts.
Fix the date of the population so a later completeness check has something to measure against.

title.en: Apply the threshold and the risk factors to every line

description.en: Run both tests over the whole population, not only the large balances, so a small account carrying heavy estimation or fraud exposure is visible as a deliberate decision.

text.en: Measure each account and disclosure against performance materiality and mark the result on the line.
Assess each line for estimation, judgement, complexity, related party volume and fraud susceptibility.
Bring sub-threshold lines into scope where a risk factor demands it, naming the factor on the line.
State a reason against every exclusion rather than leaving the line blank.
Total the excluded balances and compare the aggregate with performance materiality.

title.en: Map each in-scope account to its process, location and assertions

description.en: Convert the scoped list into something testable by naming the process that produces each balance, the location or entity it is produced in, and the assertions at risk there.

text.en: Name the process that produces each in-scope account or disclosure.
Identify the locations or entities contributing to the balance and their share of it.
State the assertions at risk for each account, such as existence, valuation or cut-off.
Flag accounts with no process owner, since those cannot be tested as they stand.

title.en: Amend the scope when an acquisition or system change lands

description.en: Scope set once a year goes stale the moment the group changes shape; this is the in-period act that keeps the scoped population matching the business that is actually reporting.

evidenceHint.en: The dated scope amendment raised for each in-period acquisition, disposal or system migration, showing the accounts added or removed and who approved the change.

text.en: Monitor acquisitions, disposals and finance system migrations announced during the period.
Assess each for the accounts, disclosures and locations it adds to or removes from scope.
Raise a dated amendment to the scoping matrix rather than waiting for the next annual run.
Inform control owners whose testing population changes as a result of the amendment.

title.en: Reconcile the approved scope against the prior year

description.en: Every account that left scope and every account that entered it is a decision someone has to stand behind, and the year-on-year comparison is where an unexplained disappearance shows up.

text.en: Compare this year's scoped list line by line with the prior year's approved scope.
Obtain a reason for each account or disclosure that entered or left the scope.
Challenge removals where the balance or the risk factor behind it has not actually changed.
Present the reconciled scope to the CFO for approval and record the date it was given.

templates.title: Risk register maintained with assigned ownership
templates.description: One standing record of the exposures capable of causing a material misstatement, each entry held by a named individual with the authority to act on it.
templates.objective: To ensure the exposures bearing on reliable financial reporting sit in one current register, each held by a named individual with authority to act rather than by a function label.
templates.successCriteria:
A single register holds the population, with no unit or project log carrying an exposure that never reaches it.
Every entry names an individual owner who holds the budget or decision rights to act, not a department or a vacant post.
Each entry carries a last review date falling within the refresh interval the register sets for itself.
Entries retired in the period record who agreed the retirement and on what basis.
Ownership moves on a leaver or a reorganisation, leaving no entry standing against someone who has gone.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register export as held at the test date, with its field list and the refresh interval it states.
Collect any unit, subsidiary or project risk log kept outside the central register.
Obtain the HR leaver and reorganisation record covering the period under test.
Request the retirement records for every entry closed during the period.
Obtain the refresh correspondence for the quarters in scope: who was asked, who replied and what changed.

Analysis:
Trace a sample of twenty-five exposures from the unit logs into the register and account for each that never arrived.
Test every sampled register entry for an individual owner, then check that person is still employed and still holds the remit the entry assumes.
Measure each entry's last review date against the test date and against the interval the register states.
Inspect retirements for a recorded approver and a stated basis, and search later refreshes for the same exposure re-entered under a new code.
Compare the leaver list against the owner column across the whole register, not only the sample.

Output:
Statement of whether one register holds the population, naming any exposure found only in a unit log.
Schedule of entries carrying no individual owner, a departed owner, or a review date beyond the stated interval.
Findings on retirements without an approver or a basis, with the entry code and responsible owner against each.

title.en: Scope what the register holds and at what grain

description.en: Settle the admission rule and the shape of an entry, so the register is a defined population rather than whatever people happened to submit.

text.en: State the admission rule: an exposure belongs in the register when it could cause a material misstatement in the reported figures.
Agree the grain of an entry, so one exposure occupies one row instead of being split across its cause and its effect.
Settle the fields every entry must carry, including owner, inherent rating, response status and last review date.
Identify the unit and project logs that feed the register, so an exposure raised in a subsidiary has a route in.
Publish the admission rule alongside the register, so a submitter can tell before writing whether an item qualifies.

title.en: Assign an individual with authority to every entry

description.en: Replace function labels in the owner field with a person who controls the process the exposure arises in, and secure that person's acceptance.

text.en: Match each entry to the individual who controls the process or system the exposure arises in.
Confirm the proposed owner holds the budget or the decision rights needed to act on that exposure.
Substitute a person for every department name, committee or vacant post currently sitting in the owner field.
Obtain each owner's written acceptance of the entries assigned, so the assignment is agreed rather than assumed.
Nominate a deputy for entries whose owner is the only person able to act on them.

title.en: Update entries each quarter and retire what is closed

description.en: Run the quarterly cycle that puts a current rating, response status and review date on every live entry, and closes the ones the owner reports as finished.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's register export showing a review date and reviewer against each live entry, together with the retirement records naming who agreed each closure and why.

text.en: Circulate each owner's entries ahead of the quarterly cut-off and ask for confirmation or amendment.
Update the rating, response status and review date on every entry an owner returns.
Retire the entries an owner reports as closed, capturing who agreed the closure and the basis given.
Enter exposures raised by incidents, audit findings or unit logs since the previous refresh.
Mark entries no owner answered for, so silence is not carried forward as confirmation.

title.en: Examine the register for gaps and stale entries

description.en: Look for what the register is missing and what it has stopped noticing, using sources outside the refresh cycle itself.

text.en: Compare the period's incidents, audit findings and control failures against the register for exposures never entered.
Pick out entries whose rating has not moved across several refreshes despite change in the underlying process.
Test whether the owners named still hold the roles their entries assume, using the current organisation chart.
Report the gaps and stale entries to the audit committee with an owner and a remediation date against each.

templates.title: Risk assessment performed at least annually
templates.description: A scheduled entity-wide identification and analysis of what threatens the financial reporting objectives, run at a fixed point in the year rather than after something has gone wrong.
templates.objective: To ensure threats to the financial reporting objectives are identified and analysed on a fixed yearly cycle covering every reporting unit, not only when an incident forces the question.
templates.successCriteria:
The cycle completed within its stated period, with a start date and a dated sign-off by management.
Objectives were settled before identification began, and each analysed exposure is expressed against one of them.
Every unit, process and location in scope contributed, and a silent unit was chased rather than counted as a nil return.
Exposures carried from the previous cycle were each re-rated, closed with a reason, or carried forward with one.
The conclusions reached the register and the year's control planning before that planning closed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the assessment calendar naming the cycle dates and the units, processes and locations in scope.
Collect the participation record: who was invited, who contributed and what each returned.
Obtain the working papers showing the financial reporting objectives the exposures were analysed against.
Request the previous cycle's exposure list with the disposition recorded against each entry this year.
Obtain management's sign-off and the date the conclusions passed to the register and to control planning.

Analysis:
Compare contributing units against the scope list and establish what was done about each unit that returned nothing.
Test whether every analysed exposure is tied to a stated reporting objective rather than to a general business worry.
Trace all previous-cycle entries to a re-rating, a closure or a carried-forward reason, examining ten closures for their basis.
Set the sign-off date against the date control planning closed, to judge whether the output arrived early enough to change it.
Examine whether changes in operations, systems, personnel and accounting standards since the last cycle were considered.

Output:
Statement of whether the cycle completed inside its stated period, naming the start and sign-off dates.
List of in-scope units that did not contribute, with the follow-up recorded for each.
Schedule of previous-cycle exposures carrying no disposition in this cycle.
Finding on whether the conclusions reached the register and the control plan before planning closed.

title.en: Schedule the annual exercise and fix the units it covers

description.en: Settle the date the assessment runs and the population it must reach, so coverage can be measured afterwards against a list written beforehand.

text.en: Place the cycle in the calendar far enough ahead of control planning for its output to change the plan.
Enumerate the reporting units, processes and locations in scope, naming the basis for excluding any.
State the financial reporting objectives the exposures will be assessed against before identification starts.
Nominate the participant from each unit who can speak for its processes and its recent changes.
Agree what a complete return looks like, so a thin submission is visibly incomplete.

title.en: Assemble the change pack each unit assesses against

description.en: Put in front of participants what has actually changed since the last cycle, so identification starts from evidence rather than from memory.

text.en: Pull the period's system implementations, process redesigns and organisational changes from the change record.
Add the accounting standards and reporting requirements that came into force or were amended.
Attach the incidents, restatements, audit findings and control failures the period produced.
Carry forward the previous cycle's exposures with their ratings, so each is revisited rather than rediscovered.
Issue the pack to every nominated participant ahead of the session, with the date it was sent.

title.en: Run the identification and analysis across every unit

description.en: Hold the sessions or collect the returns that produce rated exposures for each unit in scope, chasing the units that stay silent.

evidenceHint.en: The participation record for the cycle showing the return from each in-scope unit, the rated exposures it produced, and the chase correspondence for any unit that did not reply.

text.en: Hold the session or collect the return from each unit named in the scope list.
Capture each exposure against a stated objective, with its cause and the process it arises in.
Rate inherent likelihood and impact at the session, so a rating is not invented afterwards by the coordinator.
Chase every unit that has not returned by the cut-off and record the outcome of the chase.
Merge duplicate exposures raised by more than one unit into a single entry naming both sources.

title.en: Reconcile this cycle's conclusions against last year's

description.en: Account for every exposure the previous cycle carried and show where this cycle's output landed, so the annual run is a continuation rather than a restart.

text.en: Place the previous list beside the current one and mark each entry re-rated, closed or carried forward.
Question closures that carry no basis, and exposures that vanished without being closed at all.
Examine ratings that fell while the underlying process was unchanged, and ask what evidence moved them.
Confirm the conclusions were entered in the register and cited in the control plan, with dates for both.
Present the reconciliation to management for sign-off, naming the unresolved items.

templates.title: Risk criteria defined and applied consistently
templates.description: One published scale for likelihood, impact and tolerance, anchored to reported figures and used the same way by every unit that rates an exposure.
templates.objective: To ensure exposures are rated against one published scale anchored to reported figures, so two units facing the same facts arrive at the same rating and the same escalation.
templates.successCriteria:
A documented scale defines every likelihood and impact band in terms a rater can apply without deciding what the band means.
Impact bands are anchored to figures, such as a percentage of pre-tax income or revenue, rather than to adjectives alone.
Every unit rates against that published scale, with no local variant, rescaled matrix or private spreadsheet in use.
A sample of entries re-scored from the recorded facts reproduces the band the register holds.
Breaches of the tolerance threshold escalate by the rule the criteria state, not at the rater's discretion.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the criteria document defining the likelihood bands, the impact bands and the tolerance threshold.
Collect the rating matrix each unit actually uses, including any local spreadsheet or amended copy.
Obtain the entries rated or re-rated during the quarters under test, with the facts recorded behind each rating.
Request the calibration material and the attendance record for the people who rate.
Obtain the escalation record for entries that crossed the tolerance threshold.

Analysis:
Test whether each impact band is anchored to a figure, such as a percentage of pre-tax income or a currency amount, rather than to an adjective alone.
Compare every unit's matrix against the published one band by band, to expose rescaled or renamed variants.
Re-score a sample of thirty entries from the recorded facts and set the band reached against the band held.
Pair entries from different units describing the same exposure and compare the ratings each received.
Check all tolerance breaches in the period against the escalation rule and identify those never escalated.

Output:
Statement on whether a single scale is in use, naming each unit found operating a variant.
Re-scoring results giving the count of entries whose band could not be reproduced and the size of each difference.
Schedule of paired cross-unit exposures whose ratings diverge, with the divergence stated in bands.
List of tolerance breaches that did not escalate by the stated rule, with the entry and rater named.

title.en: Express the impact bands as figures from the accounts

description.en: Define each band by a measurable quantity tied to the financial statements, so a rater reads a threshold instead of interpreting an adjective.

text.en: State each impact band as a percentage of pre-tax income, as a percentage of revenue, or as a currency amount.
Define the likelihood bands by frequency or probability over a stated horizon, not as vague wording.
Fix the tolerance threshold and state which combination of bands crosses it.
State the escalation the criteria require once tolerance is crossed, including who must be told and how quickly.
Reconcile the top impact band against the materiality used for the financial statements, so the two do not contradict.

title.en: Walk raters through worked examples before scoring opens

description.en: Run the people who rate through pre-agreed cases with known answers, so divergence is found and settled before the scale meets a real entry.

text.en: Prepare worked examples drawn from real entries, each with the band the criteria produce.
Take the raters through the examples and capture where their answers diverge from the criteria.
Amend any band definition that two competent raters read differently, rather than blaming the raters.
Withdraw local matrices and spreadsheets, replacing them with the single published version.
Capture attendance for each rating population, so an uncalibrated unit is visible at the next round.

title.en: Score new and changed entries against the published bands

description.en: Apply the scale at each quarterly round, recording the facts relied on so the band chosen can be re-derived by someone else.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's scoring sheet showing, for each new or changed entry, the likelihood and impact bands selected and the facts relied on to select them.

text.en: Select the likelihood and impact band for every entry added or amended in the quarter.
Capture the facts behind each band, such as loss history, transaction volume or exposure value.
Route entries that cross tolerance to the escalation the criteria set, on the date the band was assigned.
Refer entries the scale cannot express to the criteria owner rather than forcing them into a band.
Hold the scoring sheet with the register entry, so the rating and its basis stay together.

title.en: Test whether two units rate the same exposure alike

description.en: Take exposures that appear in more than one unit and compare the ratings given, since divergence on shared facts is the clearest sign the scale is not being applied consistently.

text.en: Identify exposures that appear in more than one unit, such as manual journal risk or spreadsheet dependency.
Compare the bands each unit assigned and quantify the divergence in bands, not in adjectives.
Re-derive the disputed ratings from the recorded facts and determine which unit departed from the scale.
Trace divergence back to its cause: an unamended local matrix, an uncalibrated rater or an ambiguous band.
Put the findings to the criteria owner with the band definitions that need rewriting.

templates.title: Risk response decisions documented and approved
templates.description: For each rated exposure, the response chosen - accept, reduce, share or avoid - recorded with its rationale and approved by someone whose authority reaches the exposure left afterwards.
templates.objective: To ensure every rated exposure carries a chosen response, a rationale for choosing it, and an approval from someone whose authority covers the residual exposure being accepted.
templates.successCriteria:
Each exposure above the response threshold carries one of the four responses, with a recorded reason for that choice.
Acceptances name an approver and a date, and that approver's delegated authority covers the residual rating accepted.
Reduction decisions name the action, the person delivering it and the date it falls due.
The residual rating expected after the response is recorded, so an acceptance is made against a figure rather than a sentiment.
A response is revisited when the rating beneath it moves, instead of standing on the original approval.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the population of register entries rated above the response threshold during the period.
Collect the response record for each: the option chosen, the rationale given and the residual rating expected.
Obtain the delegated authority schedule fixing who may approve which level of residual exposure.
Request the approval evidence behind a sample of acceptances, such as the minute, signed decision or workflow record.
Obtain the re-rating history for exposures whose rating moved after a response was approved.

Analysis:
Reconcile the response records against the population to find rated exposures carrying no decision at all.
Test a sample of twenty-five decisions for a rationale that explains the choice rather than restating the response.
Set each sampled approver against the delegated authority schedule at the residual rating they approved.
Trace reduction decisions to a named action, a named deliverer and a due date, and check which due dates have passed.
Examine exposures whose rating moved and test whether the response was reconsidered or left on its original approval.

Output:
Schedule of exposures above the threshold with no recorded response decision.
Findings on approvals taken below the authority the residual rating required, naming the approver and the entry.
List of reduction actions past their due date while the exposure is still carried as reduced.
Statement on whether responses were reconsidered when the ratings beneath them changed.

title.en: Set the response options and the approval thresholds

description.en: Decide which responses are available, at what rating a decision becomes mandatory, and which level of management may approve which residual exposure.

text.en: Define the available responses and what each means in practice, so reduce is not used to mean accept quietly.
Set the rating at which a documented response decision becomes mandatory rather than optional.
Tie each residual rating band to the level of management entitled to approve it, using the delegated authority schedule.
State what a decision record must contain: option, rationale, residual rating, approver and date.
Agree how long an approval stands before the decision must be taken again.

title.en: Route each decision to the approver its residual rating demands

description.en: Put the decision in front of the person whose delegated authority reaches the exposure that will remain, rather than the person nearest the process.

text.en: Read the residual rating off the decision record and find the matching authority level in the schedule.
Send the decision to that approver with the rationale and the facts behind the rating attached.
Block acceptance by an approver whose authority stops below the residual rating being carried.
Escalate exposures above the highest delegated band to the board or its audit committee.
Capture the approval with its date in the register entry, not only in the approver's mailbox.

title.en: Obtain the approval before an acceptance takes effect

description.en: Work the decisions as they arise, so an exposure is never carried as accepted on the strength of an approval that has not yet been given.

evidenceHint.en: The decision record for each exposure above the threshold, showing the option chosen, the rationale, the residual rating and the dated approval from the authorised approver.

text.en: Draft the decision record when an exposure first crosses the response threshold.
State the rationale in terms of cost, feasibility or appetite, rather than repeating the option's name.
Enter the residual rating the response is expected to leave, so the approver sees what is being accepted.
Hold the entry as undecided until the approval is given, rather than showing it as accepted in advance.
Attach the approval and its date to the register entry on the day it is received.

title.en: Reassess acceptances when the rating beneath them moves

description.en: An approval was given against a particular residual figure; when that figure changes the approval no longer covers what is being carried.

text.en: Pull the exposures re-rated during the period and match each to its standing response decision.
Compare the new residual rating against the rating the original approval was given for.
Return decisions whose residual rating now exceeds the approver's authority to the correct level.
Review reduction actions past their due date and decide whether the exposure is still being reduced.
Report the acceptances left standing on superseded ratings, with the entry and approver named.

templates.title: Fraud risk assessment performed at least annually
templates.description: A fraud-specific assessment run on a stated annual cycle, covering the ways the organization's own people could misstate its reporting or take its assets.
templates.objective: To ensure the organization identifies, on a stated annual cycle, the specific ways its own people could misstate its reporting or take its assets, rather than treating error as the only threat.
templates.successCriteria:
A fraud risk assessment dated within the last twelve months exists, naming the units, accounts and processes it covered.
Each identified risk records who could commit it, the incentive or pressure behind it, and how it would be concealed.
Fraudulent reporting, asset misappropriation and corruption are each considered, or ruled out with a stated reason.
Participants are named and include people who know how the transactions actually run, not the finance function alone.
The prior assessment's conclusions are revisited against the fraud events the year produced.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current fraud risk assessment, its completion date, and the scope statement naming the units, accounts and processes covered.
Obtain the attendance record for the assessment and the role each participant held.
Collect the prior assessment and the period's fraud events: hotline reports, investigations, audit findings and any restatement.
Request the register the identified fraud risks are held in, exported at the date of test.

Analysis:
Set the completion date against the stated annual cycle and measure any overrun in months.
Sample ten identified risks, or all where fewer, and test that each records a perpetrator, an incentive or pressure, and a concealment route.
Compare the scope statement against the reporting-unit list to find units, accounts or processes excluded with no reason given.
Test that each of the three fraud types is addressed, and judge whether a type dismissed carries reasoning beyond assertion.
Trace the period's fraud events into the assessment to see whether each was anticipated by a recorded risk.

Output:
State the assessment date, the cycle claimed, and whether the cycle was met.
List identified risks missing a perpetrator, an incentive or a concealment route.
Name the units, accounts or processes outside the scope statement with no reason recorded.
Report the period's fraud events that the assessment does not reflect, with the risk that should have covered each.

title.en: Frame the annual fraud assessment around a motivated insider

description.en: Fix the scope and the working assumption before the assessment starts: which units, accounts and processes are in, and that the person being considered is inside, knows the control design and can plan around it.

text.en: List the reporting units, significant accounts and processes the assessment will cover, and the ones it will not.
State the working assumption in writing: the perpetrator is inside, knows the control design and can plan concealment.
Name the participants, covering finance, operations, IT and the people who run the transactions day to day.
Put the three fraud types in scope - fraudulent reporting, misappropriation of assets and corruption - and state how each will be evidenced.
Fix the date the assessment must complete by, measured from the completion date of the previous one.

title.en: Rate each fraud risk for incentive, opportunity and concealment

description.en: Work through the identified risks and score each on what would motivate the act, what opening exists to commit it, and how it would be kept out of sight, all before any control is credited.

text.en: Describe each fraud risk as an act: who does what, to which account, and for what gain.
Capture the incentive or pressure that would make the act attractive, such as targets, bonuses or covenant thresholds.
Identify the opening the act needs - system access, approval authority, or a gap between two people's duties.
State how the act would be concealed and how long it could run before anything surfaced.
Rate inherent likelihood and financial impact before crediting any control, and keep that inherent rating visible.

title.en: Convene the fraud workshop and capture the judgements participants signed

description.en: Run the session on the annual date, take the participants through each drafted risk, and close it with a record of what was agreed, who agreed it, and what was left open.

evidenceHint.en: Dated workshop minutes carrying the attendance list, the risks discussed, and the agreement or dissent recorded against each participant.

text.en: Circulate the drafted risk descriptions before the session so discussion starts from a draft, not a blank page.
Work through each risk in the room, recording where participants disagreed on likelihood or on coverage.
Capture risks raised in the session that were not in the draft, with the person who raised each.
Close the session with a dated attendance list and the agreed conclusion against every risk.
Assign an owner and a due date to each action the session raised.
